newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close down as EMU worries build.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close down as EMU worries build.

text.p: Italian shares ended lower on Monday following the trend on bonds and the lira which were concerned over possible delays in European economic and monetary union, but blue chips showed a more resilient performance.

France warned that it wanted a period of reflection on Europe's EMU stability pact at the European Union finance ministers' meeting in Luxembourg today, and this sent many continental European bourses into reverse with Italy following. In Milan, the focus was on telecom stocks and Parmalat.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 0.91 percent at 12,165 while Mib30 index was off just 0.01 percent at 18,221.

Italy's largest food group Parmalat ended off 5.98 percent at 2,311 lire after it confirmed it was going ahead with a C$415 million bid for Canada's Ault Foods. The shares were temporarily suspended ahead of the mid-afternoon announcement.
In telecoms, STET and Telecom Italia savings shares ended sharply lower after Treasury said savings shares would not be converted into ordinary shares.

STET ordinary shares ended up 0.38 percent at 8,546 lire after it agreed to pay 893 million marks for 29 percent stake in Serbia Telekom. TIM added 1.01 percent at 5,179 lire after Telecoms ministry announced plan to cut interconnection charges.

Oil giant ENI gained 1.38 percent at 8,859 lire after the Treasury announced at the weekend it will sell off at least a further 12.5 percent of the group later this month in the biggest international share offer seen so far this year.
Fiat up 0.48 percent at 5,835 lire ahead of Italian new car May registration data expected on Tuesday expected to show another sharp rise due to car buying incentives scheme.
